executive_summary: Across FY25 Q4 to FY26 Q3, Aptus has delivered steady AUM growth (~21–25% YoY), best-in-class profitability (ROA ~7.9%, ROE ~20%+), and stable asset quality despite conscious growth moderation. Management has proactively recalibrated strategy—exiting sub-₹7 lakh tickets, accelerating branch expansion, and tightening write-off policies—to protect portfolio quality even at the cost of near-term growth. Tone remains confident and data-driven, though growth guidance has been revised down incrementally, reflecting realism rather than denial. Key themes across calls are disciplined risk management, productivity-led scaling, and sustained margin leadership.

evidence.quote: We believe in strong growth without losing focus on the quality of the loan book and good financial metrics.
Notwithstanding seasonality, we delivered a healthy 24% year-on-year growth in AUM.
The decision to stop loans below INR7 lakhs is not due to stress but to improve customer quality going forward.
Achieving INR25,000 crores AUM by FY29 may get delayed by one or two quarters, but quality comes first.

guidance_vs_delivery.what_was_promised: AUM growth of ~28–30% in FY26 driven by branch additions and productivity
guidance_vs_delivery.what_was_delivered: AUM growth moderated to ~22% YoY by Q2FY26 as sub-₹7 lakh loans were discontinued
FY26 guidance revised to 22–24% by Q3FY26
Management acknowledged possible 1–2 quarter delay in reaching ₹25,000 cr AUM

timeline.what_was_said: Guidance revised to 22–24%; FY29 target may slip 1–2 quarters

topics.assessment: Management has progressively moderated growth guidance in response to strategic choices, signaling realism rather than over-promising.

timeline.what_was_said: Credit cost rose to ~50 bps due to write-off policy change
50 bps to be the new steady-state

topics.assessment: Increase explained transparently as a policy change; guidance stabilized thereafter.

guidance_evolution.pattern_summary: Management sets aspirational targets initially but revises them openly when strategy or environment changes, indicating credibility and prudence.

margin_commentary: Margins have been a consistent strength. Management highlighted declining cost of funds (from ~8.6% to ~8.3%) aided by repo cuts and rating upgrades, while largely retaining asset yields. Rate cuts were selectively passed on only to incremental home loans, limiting NIM impact to <10 bps. Across quarters, margin commentary has been granular and credible, supported by actual spread expansion to ~8.9% by Q3FY26.
revenue_growth_narrative: Revenue growth has been largely organic, driven by branch expansion, higher average ticket size, and productivity improvements. Management consistently cited Tier 3/4 housing demand, self-employed customer focus, and digital sourcing as growth drivers. The narrative shifted in FY26 toward quality over volume, with deliberate exit from sub-₹7 lakh loans even as it dampened short-term disbursements.
key_risks_flagged_by_management: Rising competition in affordable housing, especially from banks and SFBs (Q1FY26, Q3FY26)
Temporary stress in MSME portfolio due to end-use diversion (Q3FY26)
positive_signals: CARE rating upgrade to AA improving funding access (Q1FY26)
ROE consistently above 20%, among the highest in the sector (all quarters)
Successful expansion into Maharashtra and Odisha with improving traction (Q4FY25–Q3FY26)
Cost of funds declined by ~40 bps over FY26 (Q3FY26)
red_flags: Repeated downward revision of growth guidance (from ~30% to ~22–24%)
Visibility on monthly disbursement trends often deferred with limited quantification
Dependence on favorable rate cycle for margin expansion

business_problems_and_challenges.problem: High attrition at field officer level affecting sales and collection productivity.
business_problems_and_challenges.evidence: Management noted 40–45% attrition at field level despite low attrition at senior levels (Q4FY25, Q1FY26).

business_problems_and_challenges.problem: Manual-intensive collections management in early delinquency buckets.
business_problems_and_challenges.evidence: Management highlighted challenges in collecting more than one EMI from 30–60 DPD customers (Q1FY26).

overall_investment_signal: positive: Aptus combines superior profitability, conservative risk management, and transparent governance. While growth has moderated, this reflects strategic discipline rather than business weakness.

revenue_targets.basis: Branch expansion, ATS increase, productivity gains
